s: carriage, coach (a wagon, usually upholstered, pulled by horses)
a large automobile, especially an old-fashioned one
Kutsche.et: Borrowed from Hungarian kocsi, from the village of Kocs. Doublet of Coach.
Borrowed from French couche (“bed”), probably under influence of Kutsche (“coach”).

s: habit (a long piece of clothing worn by monks and nuns)
a jeans or leather jacket covered with band patches
Kutte.et: From Middle High German kutte (“monk habit”), from Medieval Latin cotta (“undercoat, tunic”), from Proto-Germanic *kuttô (“cowl, woolen cloth, coat”).

Kutter.et: Borrowed from English cutter, from to cut.

Kuttel.et: From Middle High German kutel, from Old High German kwedilla, from Proto-Germanic *kweþuz (“stomach, belly”).

s: to drive: to ride a carriage, to go by carriage
to drive: to go by car, to drive a car, etc.
to drive: to convey someone by carriage
to drive: to convey someone by car, etc.
Gut, ich kutschiere dich zum Bahnhof, aber du bezahlst das Benzin.
Okay, I'll drive you to the train station, but you pay for the gas.

Kutschera.et: From Czech Kučera, from kučera (“lock of curly hair”).

s: Kutztown (a borough of Berks County, Pennsylvania, United States)
